firehose_news.description: Coinbase announced a 14% workforce reduction (700 positions) on May 5, 2026, citing AI automation as justification. The layoffs come amid a 50% Bitcoin decline from October 2025 peak ($125K to $62K) and 30% year-over-year drop in trading volumes. The restructuring targets $120M-$150M in annual operating expense savings against $50M-$60M one-time charges. Q1 2026 revenue fell 5% YoY to $1.6B despite the company holding $7.5B in cash.

firehose_news.title: CMS To Offer Wegovy To Eligible Medicare Patients At $50 Monthly Copay Starting July 2026
firehose_news.description: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services announced a new Medicare GLP-1 Bridge program launching July 1, 2026, providing eligible Medicare beneficiaries with access to Novo Nordisk's Wegovy (semaglutide) at a $50 monthly copay. The program covers all doses and formulations through 2027. Additionally, Amazon Pharmacy expanded access to oral Ozempic with same-day delivery in nearly 3,000 U.S. cities and plans to introduce in-office pickup kiosks at select One Medical locations.

firehose_news.title: Here's Why UPS Stock Is Rising and Falling in 2026
firehose_news.description: UPS stock remains flat in 2026 despite April gains, facing headwinds from its voluntary 50% reduction in Amazon deliveries through mid-2026. While the company expects margin recovery in the second half, near-term profitability is pressured by network adjustment costs and broader package volume declines. Amazon's new logistics service (ASCS) poses an additional competitive threat to UPS's business.

firehose_news.title: Amazon, Google, Microsoft In Focus As EU Reportedly Mulls Restricting US Cloud Providers' Access To Sensitive Data
firehose_news.description: The European Union is considering implementing regulations to restrict US cloud providers' access to sensitive government data as part of its upcoming 'Tech Sovereignty Package' to be presented on May 27. The proposals would limit but not fully exclude foreign cloud providers from handling classified public-sector information, affecting major US tech companies. This move is driven by concerns over the US Cloud Act and strained US-EU relations under the Trump administration.

firehose_news.title: Alphabet Can Become the Most Valuable Company Thanks to Google Cloud
firehose_news.description: Alphabet is positioned to become the world's most valuable company, potentially surpassing Nvidia this year, driven by Google Cloud's impressive 63% year-over-year revenue growth and 81% net income increase in Q1. The company is demonstrating superior AI return on investment compared to competitors, with stronger profit margins and $126.8 billion in cash reserves enabling accelerated capital expenditures and market share gains. Emerging segments like Waymo and Gemini show additional long-term growth potential.

firehose_news.title: Amazon Just Announced Fantastic News for Investors: Should You Buy?
firehose_news.description: Amazon launched Amazon Supply Chain Services, allowing third-party retailers to use its delivery and logistics network. The expansion of this existing infrastructure is expected to drive revenue growth and margin expansion. With higher-margin segments like advertising (22% YoY growth) and AWS (28% YoY growth, 35% operating margin) growing faster than the core business, Amazon's operating margin could expand from 12% to ~20% over the next few years. At a market cap of $2.9 trillion and trading at 16x forward earnings, the stock is fairly valued for a megacap with strong growth prospects.

firehose_news.title: AI Stocks Were Just Put to the Test. Here's How They Fared.
firehose_news.description: AI stocks faced significant headwinds in early 2026 due to valuation concerns, with the S&P 500 Shiller CAPE ratio reaching 40 (matching dot-com bubble levels), and geopolitical uncertainty from the Iran war. However, AI stocks have rebounded strongly as tech giants demonstrated that their massive AI infrastructure spending is justified by solid customer commitments and strong revenue growth. Companies like Amazon are monetizing their $200 billion AI investments through committed customer deals, proving the long-term viability of the AI investment thesis.

firehose_news.title: Vertiv: The Backlog is Massive, the Margin of Safety is Not
firehose_news.description: Vertiv (VRT), a leader in data center power and thermal infrastructure for AI, has surged 300% in 12 months with a massive $15 billion backlog and improving unit economics. However, the stock trades at a 50.9x forward P/E multiple with only a 1.9% FCF yield, leaving minimal margin of safety despite strong fundamentals and growth prospects. The valuation assumes sustained high growth and successful services transformation, with execution risks from project delays and financing constraints.

firehose_news.title: Should You Invest in This Artificial Intelligence (AI) IPO Stock That Has a Partnership with Amazon?
firehose_news.description: X-Energy, a small modular nuclear reactor developer backed by Amazon, went public in April 2026 at $23 per share and is now trading at $31.80. While the company has secured major partnerships including a 5 GW deal with Amazon by 2039, it remains unprofitable with a $390 million comprehensive loss in 2025 and won't produce commercial products until around 2030. The analyst recommends investors consider Amazon or established clean-energy companies instead due to X-Energy's high uncertainty and competition from rivals like Oklo and NuScale.

firehose_news.title: Did Amazon Just Give This Logisitcs Stock a No-Brainer Buying Opportunity?
firehose_news.description: GXO Logistics stock plunged 18% after Amazon announced its new supply chain services business, but CEO Patrick Kelleher dismissed the threat, arguing that GXO's customized, specialized logistics solutions serve a different market than Amazon's pre-existing infrastructure offering. GXO reported strong Q1 earnings with 10.8% revenue growth and raised full-year guidance, with the CEO believing the stock sell-off presents a buying opportunity.

firehose_news.title: Generative Pulse: Earned Media Consistently Drives AI Citations, Holding at 84%
firehose_news.description: Muck Rack's third edition of its What Is AI Reading? study analyzing over 25 million links finds that earned media drives 84% of AI citations across ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini, with journalism accounting for 27% of cited sources. Paid and advertorial content represents just 0.3% of citations. Each AI platform shows distinct sourcing patterns, with ChatGPT citing Wikipedia most frequently, Claude citing PubMed Central, and Gemini citing Reddit. The findings suggest that PR and marketing teams must focus on earned media coverage to influence AI-generated answers.

firehose_news.title: Trump Administration Eyes First Official AI Dialogue With China At Beijing Summit With Xi Jinping: Report
firehose_news.description: The Trump administration is planning to initiate official AI discussions with China at a potential mid-May summit between President Trump and Xi Jinping. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent will lead the U.S. side to address risks from unpredictable AI models, autonomous weapons, and nonstate actor threats. Previous Biden-era talks produced limited progress due to China's reliance on foreign ministry rather than technical experts. The discussions come amid escalating U.S.-China tech tensions, including accusations of AI technology theft and new semiconductor export control measures.

firehose_news.title: ESET Research uncovers CallPhantom scam on Google Play: Fake logs for real money
firehose_news.description: ESET researchers uncovered 28 fraudulent Android apps called CallPhantom that falsely promised access to call logs, SMS records, and WhatsApp histories for any phone number in exchange for payment. The apps, which collectively received over 7.3 million downloads primarily targeting users in India and Asia Pacific, generated only fake data while charging users between €5 and $80 through various payment methods. Google removed all identified apps from Google Play following ESET's report.

firehose_news.title: Executives from Google, BBC, Schneider Electric and RELX Join 2026 Global Sustainability Awards Judging Panel
firehose_news.description: Sustainability Magazine and BizClik Media have announced the judging panel for the 2026 Global Sustainability Awards, taking place on 8 September 2026 in London. The panel comprises senior sustainability leaders from major global organizations including Google, Schneider Electric, BBC, Mercer, and RELX. The black-tie gala will recognize companies and executives excelling in sustainable business practices across eight award categories, with entries closing on 29 June 2026.

firehose_news.title: What Happens to Nvidia Stock If the AI Build-Out Slows Down? Here's My Answer.
firehose_news.description: The article examines potential impacts on Nvidia stock if AI growth slows. While an eventual slowdown is inevitable given the cyclical nature of the semiconductor industry, the author suggests the downside would be modest—ranging from little change to a mild 20% pullback. Nvidia's massive $4.8 trillion market cap and declining valuation multiples (forward P/E of 24) may limit downside risk. The author recommends current shareholders hold their positions, though new investors might wait for better entry points.

firehose_news.title: Snyk Embeds Anthropic's Claude to Advance AI-Powered Security for Software Development
firehose_news.description: Snyk has integrated Anthropic's Claude models into its AI Security Platform to automate vulnerability discovery, prioritization, and developer-ready fixes for AI-generated code and agentic systems. The integration addresses the accelerating challenge of securing AI-driven development, with Snyk's report showing 65-70% of production code is AI-generated and nearly half contains vulnerabilities. The solution is available to joint customers today with expanded access rolling out through 2026.

firehose_news.title: Clorox Could Be Crowned a Dividend King in 2027, But the Regal Status Will Be Short-Lived Unless Clorox Makes This Key Change.
firehose_news.description: Clorox is on track to become a Dividend King in 2027 after 48 consecutive years of dividend increases, but faces sustainability challenges. The company's dividend expense is becoming unaffordable due to declining earnings and free cash flow, despite cost-cutting efforts. While trading at an attractive 15.7x forward earnings valuation, Clorox lacks the credibility of stable dividend stalwarts like Coca-Cola and resembles 3M before its dividend cut.

firehose_news.title: Want Passive Income for Life? Buy These 3 Dividend Stocks Now.
firehose_news.description: The article recommends three dividend stocks for passive income: Procter & Gamble (70 years of dividend increases), Realty Income (monthly dividends for 55+ years with 5.1% yield), and Coca-Cola (64 consecutive years of dividend increases). All three stocks are highlighted for their stability, long track records of dividend growth, and reliability in generating consistent shareholder returns.

firehose_news.title: Bitget Launches “Fan Story: UEX Through Your Eyes” Campaign with 100,000 USDT Prize Pool
firehose_news.description: Bitget, the world's largest Universal Exchange, launched a community campaign from May 7-20, 2026 inviting users to share their Bitget experiences on social media for a chance to win up to 100,000 USDT in prizes and exclusive merchandise. The campaign aims to highlight user stories and experiences with the platform's Universal Exchange ecosystem.

firehose_news.title: Kaspi.kz: The Market’s Biggest Mispriced Monopoly--or a Hidden Fragility?
firehose_news.description: Kaspi.kz operates a dominant closed-loop digital ecosystem in Kazakhstan with exceptional network effects and platform economics, but trades at a stressed 6x forward earnings multiple due to concerns about Turkey expansion capital allocation, regulatory risks, governance issues, and accounting quality. The investment thesis hinges on whether management maintains capital discipline and the core Kazakhstan platform remains intact, or if international expansion destroys value.

firehose_news.title: S&P 500 Record Highs Leave Valuations Exposed to Any Oil Reversal
firehose_news.description: US stocks hit record highs as oil prices fall below $100 on hopes of a US-Iran peace deal that could normalize crude supplies and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The S&P 500 reached 7,384 with RSI in overbought territory, suggesting potential consolidation ahead. Labor market remains resilient with jobless claims at 200,000, though hiring is expected to slow. Mixed corporate earnings: McDonald's beat expectations while Snap and Shake Shack disappointed.

firehose_news.title: Will S&P 500 Open Up Or Down On May 7?
firehose_news.description: The S&P 500 rallied to an all-time high on May 7, 2026, climbing 1.46% to 7,365.12 as investors responded positively to reports of potential U.S.-Iran peace negotiations. Oil prices fell sharply on de-escalation hopes, boosting equities. Polymarket traders are leaning bullish for Thursday's opening, with strong corporate earnings and AI momentum supporting the rally. President Trump cautioned that no agreement has been finalized.

firehose_news.title: Nasdaq 100 Climbs Records, Oil Extends Drop As Iran Weighs Hormuz Deal: Stock Market Today
firehose_news.description: U.S. tech stocks reached record highs on May 7, 2026, as crude oil tumbled nearly 3% on hopes Iran will accept a U.S. memorandum to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The Nasdaq 100 gained 0.4% to 28,706 while the S&P 500 rose 0.2% to 7,376. Earnings drove significant stock-specific moves, with major winners including AAON (+36%), Datadog (+30%), and H&R Block (+26%), while notable losers included Planet Fitness (-33%), Insmed (-22%), and Zoetis (-22%).

firehose_news.title: 2 Outstanding AI Stocks to Buy and Hold for the Next Decade
firehose_news.description: The article recommends Microsoft and Meta Platforms as two AI stocks worth buying and holding for the next decade. Despite recent stock price declines and investor concerns about heavy AI spending, both companies are showing strong financial performance with robust revenue growth driven by AI initiatives. Microsoft's Azure posted 40% year-over-year growth and its AI business has a $37 billion annual revenue run rate, while Meta's revenue grew 33% year-over-year. Both companies are positioned to deliver excellent long-term returns despite near-term market skepticism.

firehose_news.title: Nvidia Invested $2 Billion in This Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stock. It Is Already Up 57% and Can Become a Multibagger
firehose_news.description: Nebius Group, a neocloud provider specializing in AI data centers, has surged 57% since Nvidia's $2 billion investment announcement in March 2026. With a massive $46 billion revenue backlog from deals with Meta and Microsoft, and plans to expand to 3 gigawatts of contracted power by end of 2026, analysts project the stock could triple if it achieves $16 billion revenue by 2028 at sector-average valuations.
